prompt_md: On a long road, at any moment half the vehicles are bikes at 20 km/h and half are cars at 100 km/h. A camera logs every vehicle that passes it. Average logged speed?
prompt_short: Road: half bikes at 20, half cars at 100. Average speed past a camera?
hint_md: Fast vehicles pass the camera more often.
explain_intuition_md: A snapshot of the road shows equal numbers of bikes and cars, averaging 60 km/h. But cars cover five times the distance, so five cars pass the camera for every bike. The camera's log is mostly cars, which pulls its average up to about 87.
explain_math_md: Passing rate is proportional to speed, so each speed is weighted by itself: $$\frac{20 \cdot 20 + 100 \cdot 100}{20 + 100} = \frac{10400}{120} \approx 86.7$$
